title: Sketchbook of Shadows
summary: A short text about shadows as structure rather than absence in a collection of studies.
main_text:
This set of sketches treated shadow as material, not background. Dark areas were not simply where light failed to reach. They carried weight, direction, and often the emotional center of the page. Several works would have fallen apart entirely if the shadows had been softened.

That approach changed how I read the drawings. Instead of looking first for recognizable subjects, I started by following the blackest zones and seeing what they organized around themselves. A doorway became tension. A shoulder became distance. A table edge became a dividing line between calm and uncertainty.

It reminded me that drawing is often less about outline than about subtraction. These pages were built by deciding what not to reveal fully. That made them feel intimate without becoming sentimental.
